r.정치 구도: Denmark is a parliamentary monarchy. The king is a ceremonial head of state, and the prime minister governs with the backing of the 179-seat, single-chamber parliament, the Folketing. Greenland and the Faroe Islands each hold two of those seats. Seats are allocated by proportional representation, so many parties win seats, and minority governments that bargain with other parties bill by bill are common. For decades a left bloc and a right bloc took turns in power, but in 2022 the center-left Social Democrats broke with that pattern and governed with the center-right Liberals. In the March 2026 election the Social Democrats stayed the largest party but fell to 21.9% of the vote. After 69 days of talks they formed a minority coalition in June with the Socialist People's Party, the Social Liberals and the Moderates. Two things set Denmark apart in Europe: a party of the left has led a strict immigration policy, and in 2025 parliament voted to raise the pension age to 70 by 2040.

t.why: Denmark sits on the Danish Straits, the passage between the Baltic and the North Sea. Tankers carrying Russian oil have to pass through, so since 2025 Denmark has stepped up checks on the aging shadow fleet tankers that dodge sanctions, which Moscow has called piracy. It was a founding member of NATO in 1949 and joined the European Community in 1973, but it keeps its own currency, the krone, pegged to the euro rather than adopting the euro. Voters scrapped the country's opt-out from EU defense policy in a 2022 referendum. The biggest story now is Greenland, a self-governing territory within the Danish realm. Its Arctic sea lanes, minerals and US missile warning base have led the United States to say again and again that it wants to buy the island. Tensions rose in January 2026 when Washington threatened tariffs on Denmark and seven other European countries. In September the United States, Denmark and Greenland signed a defense agreement expanding US military activity on the island, and the Danish parliament ratified it unanimously in November.
t.rel: A kingdom that includes Greenland and the Faroe Islands. In 2025-26, US talk of taking over Greenland caused diplomatic friction with the United States.
t.korea: The two countries established diplomatic relations in 1959. Before that, during the Korean War, Denmark sent the hospital ship Jutlandia, which reached Busan in March 1951 and stayed until August 1953, treating Korean civilians, more than 6,000 of them, as well as soldiers. After the war Denmark joined Norway and Sweden in founding the National Medical Center in Seoul. A green growth alliance signed in 2011 was raised in 2021 to a comprehensive green strategic partnership, the first green partnership South Korea formed with any country. Offshore wind, green hydrogen and biogas are the main areas of cooperation. Shipping is another strong tie: Maersk has ordered a string of large methanol-fueled container ships from Korean shipyards.
t.know: Denmark's flag is considered the oldest national flag still in use.
etext: Novo Nordisk grew so fast on its diabetes drug Ozempic and obesity drug Wegovy that for a while this one company drove a large share of the country's economic growth. In 2025 it lost ground to Eli Lilly of the United States and its share price fell by more than half. In September it said it would cut 9,000 jobs worldwide, about 5,000 of them in Denmark, the largest layoff in Danish history.

Denmark bet on wind power early, after the oil shocks of the 1970s, and built up the turbine maker Vestas and the offshore wind developer Ørsted. Wind supplies one of the highest shares of electricity of any country. In 2025, after the US government halted an offshore wind farm Ørsted had nearly finished, the company raised about 60 billion kroner in new shares, half of it from the state, its majority owner.

Maersk is the world's second-largest container line, and DSV became the largest freight forwarder after buying Germany's DB Schenker. When sea lanes such as the Red Sea are disrupted or freight rates jump, both companies' results swing quickly.
Pork and dairy have long been export mainstays. Danish Crown, which began as a farmers' cooperative, and Arla, owned by farmers in Denmark and Sweden, sell around the world.

Denmark is known for flexicurity: firms can lay people off easily, but unemployment benefits and retraining are generous. The tax burden is among the highest in the world. A few big companies in drugs and shipping carry so much weight that their ups and downs move the national growth rate.
